doc.title: Dave McKenna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Concord albums and their titles
summary: He credits Carl Jefferson for titles like No Bass Hit and Major League and lists his Concord duo and trio albums.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Well I like some of your album titles too, they’re creative. You had “No Bass Hit”—

I think that was, I’ve got to give Carl Jefferson credit. I think he came up with that and “Major League.” Those were the two with — “No Bass Hit” was the first one with Concord, and that was with Jake and Scott. And then I did a solo album shortly after, and “Major League” was a few years later, and for Concord I did a trio album playing that Harry Warren music, and I did an album with Gray Sargent, a duo; and an album with Joe Temperley, a duo; an album with Buddy DeFranco, a duo; a lot of duos; plus the things I did as a sideman with Cal Collins and Scott and Warren Vache and those things in Japan and so forth. So I did have, that was my longest record association, yes.
You had mentioned that there was a time in your life when you were thinking about the post office.
